Styri 2.0 brings ROS 2 and VDA 5050 robots into an offline operator panel

The free Core supports up to three robots with command logs and acknowledgements; its software stop is not a safety function.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

One local operator view

Styri has launched version 2.0, an on-site panel for ROS 2 and VDA 5050 robots. Operators can see robots on a map, send them to destinations and stop them from a browser without internet access. The Apache-2.0 Core is free for up to three robots at one site.

Status follows acknowledgement

The panel distinguishes sent, accepted, running and completed commands instead of treating transmission as completion. Viewer, operator and administrator roles accompany local command logs. Pause depends on robot support, while tablet driving is offered for ROS 2 robots.

Limits before deployment

The website reports simulator testing, with real-robot results added as testing proceeds. Styri does not provide traffic management or task allocation across vendors and runs alongside existing fleet managers. Operator stop is a software command, not a safety function or a substitute for an emergency-stop circuit.
